title: Session resume flows — lightweight UX + telemetry ideas
content:
Context:
Quick personal notes after a 1:1 and hallway convo — trying to capture lightweight ideas for a session resume UX + minimal telemetry to support it. Goal is a low-friction feature that helps apps restore conversational state (pins, highlights, short summaries) without inventing a heavy persistent-memory layer.

Top-level intent:
- Reduce user friction for multi-session conversations (chat that can resume across days/devices)
- Keep server-side cost minimal: avoid full transcript storage + re-embedding every resume event
- Provide operational signals (telemetry) to understand resume success/failure and cost impact

Problem statements (rough):
1) Users open an app after 2+ days and want the assistant to remember the gist; current patterns either repeat long context (expensive) or accept a cold start (annoying).
2) Engineers are wary of enabling long-term memory due to storage and token cost, and compliance/PII concerns.
3) Product teams want measurable metrics: how often resumes help, failure modes, and incremental token costs.

Guiding principles:
- Ephemeral-first: prefer client-side storage + optional server pinning.
- Summaries over transcripts: store short structured summaries (1–3 sentences + topical tags) instead of raw chat.
- User-controlled: explicit pin / snapshot flows rather than invisible memory.
- Cheap server ops: bounded-size records, TTLs, and delta updates to avoid re-embedding whole convo.

Feature sketch — "Session Snapshot" (name placeholder):
- What it is: a small artifact representing a conversation state at a point in time (title, 1–3 sentence summary, 3 topical tags, optional explicit pin).
- Where it lives: default local (client storage). Optional upload to Redwood-hosted resume-store (encrypted) for cross-device resume.
- How apps use it: on open, app offers user to resume from last snapshot. Server supplies snapshot->prompt prefix (short) + core metadata to decide model routing (e.g., longer prefix => route to dedicated capacity).

Minimal schema (client-server contract):
- snapshot_id: opaque string
- created_at: ISO timestamp
- title: short string (user-editable)
- summary: short string (<= 300 chars)
- tags: list of short strings (<=3)
- pointer_range: optional token index range (client only)
- confidence: optional score from local summarizer (0–1)
- persistence: enum [local, server-ttl-30d, server-ttl-90d, pinned]
- source_hint: enum [user-saved, auto-generated, system-flagged]

Operational constraints / cost model:
- If stored server-side, snapshots are tiny (few hundred bytes), but resuming will append the summary as context + optionally a short extract. Budget impact: +~X tokens per resume (estimate 30–120 tokens) vs full transcript (500–2000 tokens).
- Defaults: server TTL 30d, pinned requires explicit user acknowledgement and appears in account settings.

Resume UX flows (3 patterns):
1) Quick resume (client-only): client presents last snapshot overlay; if accepted, injects the summary into system prompt and continues. No network to Redwood required.
2) Cross-device resume (server snapshot): client requests snapshot by id, server returns encrypted summary + meta; inject into prompt and optionally request background fetch of small context extract (one paragraph).
3) Deep restore (user opt-in): server returns summary + top 1–2 relevant turns (redacted for PII by client heuristics) — used rarely, requires stronger compliance review and KMS flag.

User stories (prioritized):
- As a returning user, I want to pick up where I left off, so I don't repeat context.
- As a privacy-conscious user, I want to keep my snapshots local unless I opt into cloud sync.
- As a product manager, I want to see resume-success rate and median tokens added by resumes to evaluate cost/benefit.

Telemetry (minimal set to ship quickly):
- event.snapshot_created {persistence, source_hint, snapshot_size_bytes}
- event.snapshot_resumed {persistence, resumed_via: [client, server], tokens_added_by_resume, model_id}
- event.snapshot_deleted {method: [user, ttl, admin]}
- metric.resume_success_rate = resumed_sessions / resume_attempts
- distribution.tokens_added_by_resume (p50/p90)
- NOTE: PII rule — summaries must be flagged if they contain potential PII; we should surface a low-sensitivity classifier on client to avoid sending raw PII to telemetry.

Edge cases / open questions:
- Auto-summary quality: local summarizer vs server summarizer — tradeoffs: client reduces upload risk but might be lower quality. Is a hybrid ok (client summary up, server re-summarizes when requested)?
- Relevance decay: how to auto-evict / collapse snapshots that are stale or no longer relevant? TTL + usage-based promotion (if resumed repeatedly extend TTL).
- Compliance: pinned snapshots may need stronger retention controls and audit logs. How do we expose export/delete for DSAR?
- Migration: customers using existing memory APIs — how to interop with Redwood's caching/batching?

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create snapshot API (client-only flow documented) + simple client SDK helper that serializes snapshot to localStorage (web) and optional native store.
- Server-side resume store API (opt-in) with TTL 30d and HIPAA/PII notes in docs.
- Telemetry events emitted for create/resume/delete. Dashboard prototype showing resume_success_rate and token delta distribution.
- UX: lightweight UI modal for resume with summary, tags, and quick "edit" link.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Users accidentally store sensitive info in server snapshots. Mitigation: default to local-only, explicit opt-in for server, client-side PII warn, and blur UI copy.
- Risk: Snapshot abuse (large user base writes many small objects). Mitigation: quota by snapshots/day + size cap + TTL.
- Risk: Quality mismatch leading to poor user experience. Mitigation: A/B testing of resume vs cold start, collect examples for evaluation, early canary to customers who opt in.

Implementation notes / engineering prompts:
- Server store: design as key-value with small metadata indices; make snapshot retrieval O(1) with a small index per user. Prefer provisioned capacity pathways for heavy resume rates.
- SDK helpers: web + iOS + Android templates for local snapshot lifecycle and UI components.
- Model prompt pattern: system_prompt +=
  "Previous session summary: <summary>
  If user reveals <sensitive-patterns> follow privacy policy..."
- Hook for routing: if tokens_added_by_resume > threshold, mark request as candidate for dedicated capacity routing to avoid latency spikes.

Next steps (short):
- Share with Maya + Evan for early feedback (they were in 1:1).
- Quick spike: client-only local snapshot demo (web) within 1 week.
- Telemetry proto: define events and simple dashboard mock in Console.
- Bring to product sync for prioritization, aim for small canary with 5 customers.

Notes to self: keep the initial scope tiny. Focus on discovery/measurement first — if resume doesn't move retention or reduce tokens, we stop. Also, keep language in UX explicit about where data is stored (local vs cloud).
